title: SURVEYING ATTITUDINAL ALIGNMENT BETWEEN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS VS. HUMANS TOWARDS 17 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing existing literature to compare LLM outputs, decision-making criteria, and data-driven recommendations against human emotional, ethical, and contextual perspectives across the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Synthesizing literature on LLM performance in occupational predictions, the generation of clinical vignettes, and the drafting of recommendation letters to identify ingrained stereotypes and outcome disparities.
Surveying studies that evaluate AI and LLM outputs for stereotyping in healthcare diagnoses, treatment plans, and error rates in facial recognition technologies among different racial groups.

Analyzing literature on how LLMs process local contexts, languages, and traditional knowledge, highlighting the overrepresentation of mainstream or Western cultures and the marginalization of rural and underdeveloped regions.

Evaluating how LLMs conceptualize poverty and inequality primarily through quantifiable economic and algorithmic metrics, often overlooking underlying social complexities, lived experiences, and power structures.

Reviewing empirical studies that test LLM responses to political prompts to identify ideological tendencies, such as exhibiting left-leaning liberal preferences or favoritism toward specific political parties.
